meta.title: The Bus That Leaves Early
meta.skill_frame: Find the main idea: decide what a passage is mostly about.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a third-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: The load is one change and one response. Every sentence supports the same point: the start time moved. Measured FK 3.2-3.9 on the two parts (Flesch-Kincaid, approximate syllable count). The reading load sits inside the grade 2-3 band and below the 4.1 floor, which measures 5.3 at its easiest.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for main_idea 3.1, band 3.1, sequence 1. No external work.
source.survey: Written to the floor: short sentences, everyday words, one or two links.
source.avoided: No childish subject. No talking down. No invented facts about real named places.

session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance and number of links, climbing one knob per sequence.

authoring_exceptions: Parts run 55-85 words instead of 100-200. At band 3.1 the text is short by design: two parts keep the session inside 12 minutes and the load stays at one or two links. Recorded under 2.1.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: Route 12 used to leave the square at 7:10 every morning. In March it started leaving at 7:05 instead. The bus cannot wait past the light on Third Street, and that light now stays red for a long time. So the bus pulls out five minutes early to stay on time. The new time is printed on the sign at the stop.
passage.part_2: Riders noticed the change right away, and some missed the bus for a week. The transit office put a note on the sign and sent a text to people on the route. The ride itself has not changed, and the fare has not changed. The bus still reaches the hospital by 7:40. Only the start time moved.

items.prompt: What is the first part mostly about?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The bus now leaves five minutes early, and why.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Every sentence in the first part serves one point: the new 7:05 start and the red light behind it.
tutor_only.tell: The first part is about the new start time and the reason for it.
help: Look at what every sentence in the first part is about.
The time, the light, and the sign all point to one thing.
tutor_only.core_idea: The bus now leaves five minutes early, and the red light is why.
accept_ideas: it leaves five minutes early because of the light

if_they_say.when: the student says it is about a red light
if_they_say.ask: The light is one reason inside a bigger point. What is the whole first part about?

items.prompt: What is the second part mostly about?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. Riders and the office adjusted to the new time.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The second part moves from riders missing the bus to the sign and text, then says nothing else changed.
tutor_only.tell: The second part is about people getting used to the earlier time.
help: Look at what the riders, the note, and the text have in common.
The last sentences say what did not change. What did?
tutor_only.core_idea: People adjusted to the new start time.
accept_ideas: how people dealt with the new time
not_required: the number of the text message

if_they_say.when: the student says it is about the fare
if_they_say.ask: The passage says the fare did not change. What is the second part about?

items.prompt: What is the whole passage mostly about?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. One route changed its start time, and people dealt with it.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Both parts serve one idea: the 7:05 start. The first explains it, the second shows the response.
tutor_only.tell: One bus route started leaving five minutes early. Riders adjusted.
help: Both parts are about the same time change.
One part explains it. The other shows what people did.
tutor_only.core_idea: One bus route moved its start time five minutes earlier, and riders adjusted.
accept_ideas: one route changed its start time
the bus leaves five minutes early now
a schedule change on one route
the bus start time changed and people adjusted

if_they_say.when: the student says it is about buses in general
if_they_say.ask: The passage follows one route and one change. What is it?

items.prompt: What time does Route 12 leave now?

tutor_only.correct_reason: The second sentence gives the new time.
tutor_only.tell: It leaves at 7:05, five minutes earlier than before.
help: Find the sentence with the new time.

if_they_say.ask: That was the old time. What does the passage say it is now?

items.prompt: The passage says the fare did not change. Is that the main idea? Explain.

tutor_only.confirm: Right. It is one detail, not the main idea.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The main idea is the schedule change. The fare appears once, to show what stayed the same.
tutor_only.tell: One sentence about the fare does not carry the passage. The time change does.
help: Count how many sentences are about the fare.
Then look at how many are about the time.
tutor_only.core_idea: No. It is one detail; the passage is about the start time.
accept_ideas: no, it is a supporting detail
no, the main idea is the time change

if_they_say.when: the student says yes because the fare is mentioned
if_they_say.ask: One mention does not make a main idea. How many sentences are about the time?
